title: Closed-point topology of integral representable stack morphisms
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal V$ be an algebraic stack of finite type over $k$ with quasi-compact separated diagonal [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], and let $h:\mathcal N\to\mathcal V$ be a representable integral morphism of algebraic stacks. Here integral means that for every scheme $T\to\mathcal V$ the $2$-fibre product $\mathcal N\times_{\mathcal V}T$ is a scheme integral over $T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Point spaces and their topologies are [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. The continuous map $|h|$ sends closed subsets to closed subsets. If $v\in|\mathcal V|$ is a closed point, then every $n\in|\mathcal N|$ with $h(n)=v$ is a closed point of $|\mathcal N|$. No finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal N$, and $h$ need not be surjective.

source.place: Tags 0CHU (definition-integral) and 0512 (lemma-characterize-representable-universally-closed), with spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0415 (lemma-integral-universally-closed). Closed-fibre assertion: Tag 0H27 (lemma-residual-space-closed), Tag 0H22 (lemma-every-point-residual-gerbe-locally-Noetherian), and morphisms.tex Tag 02NT (lemma-integral-fibres), applied after a field presentation of the closed residual gerbe. The finite-type stabilizer has finitely many connected components, so its orbits on the zero-dimensional integral field fibre are finite closed subsets. This spells out the assertion used when Alper Lemma 8.3.1 says that its open immersion preserves closed points.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal V$ and put $X_U=\mathcal N\times_{\mathcal V}U$. By hypothesis $X_U$ is a scheme integral over $U$, so $X_U\to U$ is closed by the integral/universally-closed criterion. If $C\subseteq|\mathcal N|$ is closed, its inverse image $C_U$ in $|X_U|$ is closed by continuity. The base-change image assertion gives $|p|^{-1}(|h|(C))=\operatorname{im}(C_U\to|U|)$, which is closed. The atlas criterion on $\mathcal V$ therefore makes $|h|(C)$ closed. This proves the first assertion without a finiteness assumption on $\mathcal N$.

source.place: Tags 04XL (lemma-topology-points) and 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian); morphisms.tex Tag 01WM (lemma-integral-universally-closed); the atlas argument of stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0512.

proof.text: Fix a closed point $v$ of $|\mathcal V|$. Let $i:\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal V$ be the reduced closed substack with $|\mathcal Z|=\{v\}$. It is locally of finite type over $k$ by closed-immersion calculus. Its reduced smooth scheme charts are locally of finite type over $k$, hence locally Noetherian: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field, and the locally-Noetherian finite-type lemma applies to these charts. Thus the singleton field-cover lemma supplies a representable surjective flat locally finitely presented map $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal Z$. Only the target substack $\mathcal Z$, not $\mathcal N$, is being declared locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0509 (lemma-reduced-closed-substack); stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 06FV, 06FT and 06R6; Tag 06MP (lemma-unique-point-better); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal M=\mathcal N\times_{\mathcal V}\mathcal Z$ and $X=\mathcal N\times_{\mathcal V}\operatorname{Spec}K=\mathcal M\times_{\mathcal Z}\operatorname{Spec}K$. Closed-immersion calculus makes $\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ a closed immersion, and the base-change image assertion identifies $|\mathcal M|$ with $|h|^{-1}(\{v\})$. The scheme $X$ is integral over $K$, hence affine, say $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Every point of $X$ is closed: if primes $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ of $B$ are comparable, both contract to $0$ in $K$, so integral incomparability makes them equal. Thus every prime is maximal and its Zariski closure is its singleton. The projection $q:X\to\mathcal M$ is surjective flat locally finitely presented by base change of $a$. Its point map is an open continuous surjection, hence a quotient map.

source.place: Tags 0501, 0H20, 04XH and 04XL; stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06Q4; morphisms.tex Tag 02NT (lemma-integral-fibres), whose proof is integral incomparability.

proof.text: For $x\in X$ put $L=\kappa(x)$ and $E=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_{\mathcal M}X$. Since $X=\mathcal M\times_{\mathcal Z}\operatorname{Spec}K$, associating fibre products identifies $E=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_{\mathcal Z}\operatorname{Spec}K$. This also equals $\operatorname{Spec}L\times_{\mathcal V}\operatorname{Spec}K$: the closed immersion $i$ is fully faithful, so an isomorphism of the two images in $\mathcal V(T)$ is uniquely an isomorphism in $\mathcal Z(T)$. Thus $E$ is the base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal V/k}$ by $\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_kK)$, and is quasi-compact by the assumed quasi-compactness of that diagonal and its defining scheme test. Choose an affine surjective etale scheme chart $W\to E$ by the quasi-compact-space atlas lemma. The map $E\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is a base change of $a$, hence locally finitely presented. Chartwise calculus makes $W\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ locally of finite type. Since $W$ is affine it is of finite type over $L$ and is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma. Its topological space is Noetherian by the Noetherian-space topology lemma. The base-change image assertion and surjectivity of $W\to E$ show that the image of $W\to X$ is exactly $|q|^{-1}(\{|q|(x)\})$.

source.place: Tag 04XH (lemma-points-cartesian); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover); stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06Q4; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6; spaces-properties.tex Tag 04ZF (Noetherian topology). The fibre-product identification is direct from the triples definition.

proof.text: The Noetherian topological space $W$ has finitely many irreducible components. Each component has a generic point $\eta$ because $W$ is a scheme. If $w$ lies in that component, then $w\in\overline{\{\eta\}}$, and continuity of $W\to X$ gives $f(w)\in\overline{\{f(\eta)\}}=\{f(\eta)\}$, the last equality holding because every point of $X$ is closed by step 3. The image of each component is therefore one point. Consequently $|q|^{-1}(\{|q|(x)\})=f(|W|)$ is a finite set of closed points, hence closed in $X$. This argument uses no Noetherian hypothesis on $X$.

source.place: Topology Tag 0052 (finite irreducible-component decomposition); schemes.tex Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober); continuity is Tag 04XL. The specialization calculation is the explicit finite-image argument.

proof.text: Since $|q|$ is a quotient surjection, the closedness of $|q|^{-1}(\{|q|(x)\})$ proves that $|q|(x)$ is closed in $|\mathcal M|$. Surjectivity provides such an $x$ over each point of $\mathcal M$, so every point of $\mathcal M$ is closed. The closed immersion $\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ sends these closed singletons to closed singletons in $|\mathcal N|$. As its image is exactly $|h|^{-1}(\{v\})$, this proves the second assertion, including the case of an empty fibre.

source.place: Tag 0H20 (lemma-subspace-induced-topology), combined with the quotient topology of Tag 04XL.

proof_origin.place: Assembly from Tags 04XH, 04XL, 0509 and 06MP; finite-image specialization argument using schemes.tex 01IS, Topology 0052 and morphisms.tex 02NT. This replaces the informal stabilizer-orbit explanation in the item source by an explicit field-relation chart calculation.
